acceptance_criteria: One CA-trusted or managed QuickPLS leaf certificate is approved by exact subject and SHA-1 thumbprint and bound into every candidate.
Private signing material is hardware-backed or service-managed and is not stored in the repository.
Desktop, CLI, and final installer are SHA-256 Authenticode signed and RFC 3161 timestamped.
SignTool and Windows APIs verify trust, timestamp, exact approved leaf, QuickPLS product/version identity, and every signature without warnings.
Durable candidate copies are rehashed and reverified after copying and match the accepted source binaries exactly.
Clean offline install and first launch pass on the oldest supported and current patched Windows releases.
Standard-user and administrator paths complete sample or import, calculation, export, save, and reopen.
The documented WebView2 strategy works without an undisclosed network prerequisite.
N-1 upgrade preserves supported projects, results, settings, and recovery state.
Interrupted or failed upgrade has a tested recovery or full-installer fallback without data loss.
Uninstall removes application-owned binaries, shortcuts, registry entries, and processes while preserving user projects by default.
Portable and installed editions coexist without corrupting shared user state.
Unattended installation, uninstall, and exit codes are documented and tested.
The manual updater contains the exact full installer plus a detached-CMS channel manifest signed by the approved QuickPLS leaf.
Beta and stable manifests bind channel, payload identity, version floor, installer/recovery hashes, and automatic downgrade rejection.
Update checking is manual by default and its network behavior is disclosed.
Signature failure, interruption, retry, rollback, and offline full-installer recovery are tested.
A monitored support channel, severity definitions, response targets, supported-version policy, and escalation owner are published.
Known issues, rollback guidance, and a private security-reporting route are current for the target release.
Versioned system requirements, installation, update, uninstall, scope, tutorial, citation, release-note, and troubleshooting documentation are published.
User-initiated diagnostics exclude datasets, project contents, secrets, and full personal paths by default.
A privacy notice covers offline processing, manual update checks, distribution-site logs, diagnostics, and support submissions.
Packaged network tests prove that the QuickPLS application and page make no undisclosed telemetry or automatic external launch-time request.

Published claims distinguish QuickPLS application/page behavior from Microsoft-managed WebView2 process behavior; fully-offline, no-telemetry, and zero-egress claims remain blocked until an OS-enforced fixed-WebView2 containment gate passes.
Threat review covers hostile data/project files, archive abuse, formula injection, active exports, file paths, Tauri IPC, updater, and signing keys.
Release-blocking findings are closed and dependency, advisory, secret, and license checks pass.
Qualified review covers EULA, source-available license, notices, privacy, trademark, comparative claims, liability, and institutional distribution.
The checked-in disposition identifies reviewer, date, scope, and stable confidential-record reference without exposing privileged material.
Independent reviewers with documented qualifications assess the target release's high-risk method families, declare relevant conflicts, and record review scope and disposition.
Every scientifically material finding is closed, release-blocking, or explicitly resolved through a bounded documented claim before approval.
The exact release has an actual CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM with package identifiers, licenses, and a complete dependency graph plus reviewed third-party license inventory.
Critical or high dependency advisories have an approved resolution or documented release-blocking disposition.
An in-toto/SLSA provenance statement binds the protected clean build, source commit, lockfiles, toolchain, candidate subjects, SBOM, signatures, and signed build attestation.
The exact tested signed hashes are promoted to the immutable stable tag and release.
A privacy-safe external cohort includes experienced SmartPLS users and researchers new to SEM across at least five independent institutions or groups.
At least 15 participants complete at least 30 real workflows and at least 90 percent of designated core journeys finish without developer intervention.
No unresolved P0 or P1 defect, reproducible data loss, or archive corruption remains.

Scientifically material discrepancies are disposed and a structured lifecycle report rehashes the exact signed candidate manifest, artifacts, signature reports, and all mandatory recovery phases after beta fixes.
Internal, beta, and stable channels have distinct labels, manifests, eligibility rules, and rollback paths.
Public comparison claims link to current evidence and do not imply complete parity, identity, project compatibility, or affiliation.
